RenderFormer takes a scene made of triangles and predicts an image with lighting and shadows.
Its name may be unfamiliar, but it starts with the attention mechanism used in language models.

This video has two main parts.

Next, we will examine what changes when the inputs are triangles instead of words.
The key is a two-stage process: organize the scene, then form an image for a particular camera view.
Finally, we will review the training scenes, results, and conditions this approach still struggles with.
